overview: Akamai is a global technology company founded in 1998 that operates one of the internet's largest distributed networks (4,300+ edge points-of-presence in 130+ countries) to deliver security, cloud computing/compute, and content delivery solutions to enterprise and government customers. The company is in the midst of a multi-year transition away from its legacy, declining CDN ('delivery') business toward higher-growth security solutions (now its largest revenue category) and a rapidly scaling cloud/AI compute platform (Cloud Infrastructure Services), the latter now anchored by massive, debt- and equity-funded capacity commitments from AI model providers including Anthropic.

business_model.summary: Akamai sells subscription-like, multi-year contracts (typically one year or longer) across three solution categories: security (WAF, bot management, DDoS, API security, Zero Trust/microsegmentation), cloud computing (compute, storage, GPU/AI inference infrastructure - 'Cloud Infrastructure Services'), and legacy content delivery (web/mobile performance and media delivery). Revenue is largely recurring/contracted with usage-based traffic components; the business is shifting from a low-growth, high-margin legacy CDN model to a still-profitable but lower-gross-margin, capital-intensive cloud/AI compute model.

revenue_streams.name: Security
revenue_streams.detail: $2,243.4M FY2025 vs $2,042.7M FY2024, +10% YoY (+9% constant currency); largest and fastest-durable-growth category, driven by API security, WAF and Guardicore microsegmentation

revenue_streams.name: Delivery
revenue_streams.detail: $1,256.7M FY2025 vs $1,318.1M FY2024, -5% YoY; structural decline from DIY/alternative sourcing, pricing pressure at renewal, and social-media/media customer traffic optimization, partially offset by acquired Edgio/Lumen/StackPath customer contracts

revenue_streams.name: Cloud Computing (incl. Cloud Infrastructure Services)
revenue_streams.detail: $708.1M FY2025 vs $630.4M FY2024, +12% YoY; within this, Cloud Infrastructure Services (compute/storage/GPU/networking) grew from $230.0M (FY2024) to $313.9M (FY2025) and grew 39% YoY in Q2 2026 alone ($99M quarter), guided to grow at least 50% for full-year 2026

business_model.customer_type: Enterprise and government B2B; customers include Adobe, Airbnb, Comcast, EA, Marriott, NBCUniversal, Sony, Spotify, the U.S. DoD/Treasury/Labor/Transportation departments, and (new, 2026) frontier AI labs such as Anthropic. No single customer exceeded 10% of revenue in FY2023-FY2025, though the new multi-billion-dollar AI infrastructure commitments (Anthropic, an unnamed 'leading frontier model provider') are creating rapidly increasing revenue and capex concentration risk.
business_model.geographic_mix: U.S. 51% / International 49% (FY2025); no single non-U.S. country exceeds 10% of revenue

main_competitors: Hyperscaler cloud/GPU providers (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, CoreWeave, Nebius)
DIY/in-house solutions built by large customers
competitive_position.market_position: Revenue leader in enterprise CDN/security despite low website-level deployment share (roughly 3% of measured CDN site usage vs. Cloudflare's ~61%, reflecting Akamai's focus on large, complex, first-mile-critical enterprise/media/gaming/financial-services customers rather than the long tail of websites). Akamai generated ~$4.2B FY2025 revenue vs. Cloudflare's ~$2.2B and Fastly's ~$624M, underscoring a premium enterprise-grade positioning even as free-tier/self-serve competitors dominate site count. In cloud/AI compute, Akamai is a small, fast-growing entrant relative to the hyperscalers, but is differentiating via distributed edge inference and having landed marquee anchor AI customers.

moat_factors.description: 4,300+ edge PoPs across 130+ countries/~700 cities and ~1,200 network partner integrations, built over 25+ years; difficult and capital-intensive to replicate, giving Akamai unique first-mile/last-mile performance and internet visibility (attack pattern/traffic intelligence)

Multi-year enterprise contracts, deep integration into customer security and delivery architecture, and long relationships with large, complex customers (DoD, major media/gaming/financial firms) create renewal stickiness, though large customers have periodically defected to DIY
560+ U.S. patents; long track record securing and accelerating the internet's most demanding traffic; trusted by government and Fortune-level enterprises

Landmark $11.6B (potential $20B) multi-year Anthropic commitment plus other frontier-model-provider deals (aggregate >$2.8B of 2026-announced commitments) validate Akamai's distributed compute platform for AI inference workloads and could become a durable moat if capacity is scarce and demand structural

moat_factors.factor: Cost/scale disadvantage vs. hyperscalers in cloud compute
moat_factors.description: Akamai is a much smaller compute/GPU buyer than AWS/Google/Microsoft/CoreWeave, and management itself flags that large competitors have priority access to servers, memory, co-location and power, constraining Akamai's cost structure and capacity growth

weaknesses: Legacy delivery (CDN) segment (~30% of revenue) in structural, multi-year decline from DIY adoption and renewal pricing pressure, with no clear inflection
Gross margin compression as revenue mix shifts toward lower-margin cloud/compute (58.9% FY2025 gross margin down from 60.4% FY2023, and 55.8-56.1% in H1 2026)
Low market share by CDN site count versus Cloudflare's self-serve, developer-friendly, largely free platform
Heavily reliant on securing scarce, expensive GPU/data-center capacity from third parties (NVIDIA GPUs, co-location providers) where it lacks hyperscaler purchasing power
Newly concentrated exposure to a small number of very large AI infrastructure customers (Anthropic and other frontier labs) for the bulk of incremental cloud growth

growth_drivers: Security solutions growth (API security via Noname/Neosec acquisitions, WAF, Guardicore/Zero Trust microsegmentation, new Firewall for AI product) - largest and most durable growth engine

Cloud Infrastructure Services / AI compute buildout - Akamai Inference Cloud (AIC), GPU-based compute for AI inference at the edge, Kubernetes-based Akamai App Platform (built on acquired Otomi technology), Fermyon (WebAssembly serverless, acquired Nov 2025) integration

Large multi-year AI infrastructure contracts: $11.6B (with potential expansion to ~$20B) multi-year Anthropic agreement announced Sept 24, 2026; earlier $1.8B, seven-year frontier-model-provider deal (also believed to be Anthropic, first disclosed May 2026); $600M four-year robotics-focused customer deal; aggregate >$2.8B of new 2026 commitments disclosed as of Q2 2026 earnings

Security bolt-on M&A to extend product breadth - Neosec (API security, 2023), Noname Security (API security, 2024), Otomi/Red Kubes (Kubernetes app platform, 2024), Fermyon (edge WebAssembly, Nov 2025), and LayerX Security (secure enterprise browser / AI usage control, closed July 2026, ~$205M cash)
Management guidance for 2027 revenue growth to accelerate into the low-teens as new AI capacity commitments ramp (vs. mid-single-digit growth historically)
Cross-sell of security and cloud offerings into the large existing enterprise customer base

business.description: DIY adoption by large customers (e.g., a major social media customer), multi-vendor diversification, and competitive/renewal pricing pressure continue to erode the legacy CDN business, historically Akamai's core

business.risk: Intensifying competition across all three segments
business.description: Hyperscalers increasingly compete in both security and especially cloud/AI compute with far greater financial resources, priority access to compute/power/co-location, and broader platform bundling; smaller, more nimble security vendors also erode share

business.risk: Customer/revenue concentration in new AI infrastructure deals
business.description: A small number of very large frontier-AI-lab contracts (Anthropic being the most prominent, now also an Akamai shareholder via warrant) are becoming an outsized share of incremental growth and capex justification; a slowdown in AI capex cycles, customer financial distress, or contract renegotiation would disproportionately hit growth

business.risk: Execution risk in unproven compute business
business.description: Management itself flags uncertainty whether its cloud computing buildout will generate sufficient revenue/profitability to be successful, and that bugs/failures in rapidly deployed new infrastructure could damage reputation

financial.risk: Sharply increased leverage from convertible note issuance
financial.description: Total convertible note principal jumped from ~$4.1B (pre-May 2026) to $7.64B after issuing $1.75B of 0% notes due 2030 and $1.75B of 0% notes due 2032 in May 2026 (upsized from an initially proposed $2.6B); balance-sheet carrying value of debt reached ~$7.56B by Q2 2026 (current $1,705.6M + non-current $5,857.3M), a large step-change in leverage for a company with FY2025 revenue of ~$4.2B

Five tranches of convertible notes now outstanding (2027 due Sept-2027 at $116.18 conversion price now within trigger range/reclassified current, 2029, 2030, 2032, 2033) carry conversion prices from ~$93 to ~$201/share; note hedges and warrants were purchased/sold concurrently to mitigate dilution, but the 2033 tranche's conversion trigger condition being met (reclassified to current liabilities) signals the stock price is already near/above some conversion thresholds, raising near-term dilution and cash-settlement risk

Akamai issued Anthropic a warrant for up to ~5% of common shares outstanding (with ~2% vesting immediately) tied to the $11.6B commitment - an unusual customer-as-shareholder structure that dilutes existing holders and ties Akamai's equity value partly to a single counterparty relationship

financial.risk: Heavy near-term capex ramp pressures free cash flow
financial.description: Capex guided to ~40% of revenue for FY2026 (Q3 2026 capex guide $475-525M) and ~$5.5B of capex tied specifically to the Anthropic commitment; large upfront capital intensity with 6-9 month lag before contracted AI revenue is recognized
~49% of revenue is international; a weaker U.S. dollar was a modest FY2025 tailwind ($13.7M positive), but the dynamic could reverse and impact reported results

regulatory.risk: Global data privacy and localization regulation
regulatory.description: GDPR, CCPA, and a growing patchwork of data localization/digital sovereignty rules increase compliance costs and could restrict cross-border data flows core to Akamai's network operations
Rapidly evolving and inconsistent AI regulatory landscape globally could constrain how Akamai builds and offers AI inference/compute capabilities or increase compliance costs

Tariffs on servers, GPUs and networking equipment (and potential export controls on advanced computing technology) raise input costs and could disrupt the supply chain supporting Akamai's compute buildout
Some jurisdictions have adopted or proposed content-delivery restrictions, internet 'fair share' fees, or new telecom-style oversight that could affect Akamai's network operations

macro.description: Akamai's new growth narrative is now heavily levered to continued, large-scale capital spending by AI model developers (Anthropic and others); any slowdown, bubble-deflation, or financing stress in the broader AI infrastructure buildout would directly hit Akamai's largest growth driver and stranded capex

Convertible notes are largely 0%-0.375% coupon (only the 2029 notes carry a meaningful 1.125% coupon), limiting direct interest expense sensitivity, but higher-for-longer rates could pressure refinancing terms at maturity and depress the equity multiple assigned to a more capital-intensive, debt-funded growth story

macro.risk: General macro/geopolitical headwinds on enterprise IT spend
macro.description: Inflation, economic uncertainty, and geopolitical tensions (including ~6% of employees based in Israel) have historically caused customers to delay spending, optimize traffic/DIY, or lengthen sales cycles

macro.risk: Co-location, power, server/memory cost inflation driven by hyperscaler demand
macro.description: Hyperscaler-driven market dynamics are increasing co-location, GPU/server, memory, and power costs and constraining supply, directly pressuring Akamai's cost structure and capex efficiency

macro_factors.industry_outlook: CDN/delivery is a mature, slow/declining market; enterprise cybersecurity is growing at a healthy double-digit clip industry-wide; cloud/AI compute infrastructure (especially GPU-based inference) is in a period of extremely rapid, capex-heavy secular growth as frontier AI labs scale out capacity, though sustainability of that capex super-cycle is increasingly debated by the market
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - enterprise IT/security spend is relatively resilient but can be deferred in downturns; media/gaming delivery traffic has some cyclicality tied to content release schedules and events; new AI infrastructure revenue introduces new cyclicality tied to a nascent, capital-intensive, and potentially volatile AI capex cycle
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity given mostly 0%-coupon convertible debt, but high indirect sensitivity via cost of future refinancing, equity valuation multiple for a newly debt-funded growth story, and financing conditions for AI-sector customers/counterparties
key_input_costs: Servers and memory (subject to tariffs and hyperscaler-driven scarcity)
Skilled engineering/R&D and sales talent (stock-based compensation heavy)

recent_developments.event: Announced a massively expanded, $11.6 billion multi-year (7-year) agreement with Anthropic for AI compute capacity, with potential expansion to ~$20 billion total commitment; Akamai issued Anthropic a warrant for up to ~5% of common shares outstanding (~2% vesting immediately); ~$5.5 billion of associated capex expected; shares jumped as much as ~20-27% in after-hours/pre-market trading on the announcement, though the stock gave back gains and fell ~6.8% in the following regular session on capex/dilution concerns

Beat Q2 2026 estimates (non-GAAP EPS $1.59 vs. $1.58 expected; revenue ~$1.1B, +5% YoY); stock jumped ~12% on the print; Cloud Infrastructure Services revenue grew 39% YoY to $99M; disclosed new $600M, four-year robotics-focused customer commitment (no material FY2026 revenue, ramping through 2027); management guided 2027 revenue growth to accelerate into the low-teens; total 2026-announced multi-year commitments exceeded $2.8B as of the print

Closed acquisition of LayerX Security Ltd. (Israeli secure-enterprise-browser / AI usage-control vendor) for ~$205 million in cash, subject to post-closing adjustments; expected to be ~$0.12 dilutive to non-GAAP EPS for FY2026, with LayerX expected to reach ~$10M ARR by year-end 2026

Priced an upsized $3.5 billion convertible senior notes offering ($1.75B due 2030 at 0% coupon, $1.75B due 2032 at 0% coupon, including full exercise of initial purchasers' option) alongside note hedge and warrant transactions to mitigate dilution and a ~$350 million share buyback; proceeds earmarked primarily for accelerated Cloud Infrastructure Services capacity buildout, including to support the first large AI/frontier-model-provider commitment

Disclosed initial $1.8 billion, seven-year cloud infrastructure deal with an unnamed 'leading frontier model provider' (later identified as Anthropic) - Akamai's largest contract in company history at the time; stock jumped ~20-27% on the news
Acquired Fermyon Technologies (serverless WebAssembly/edge-native application platform) to deepen edge functions integration with Akamai's compute and security products

Management committed to a restructuring action (headcount reduction) to reprioritize investment toward faster-growing security and cloud computing areas; also introduced changes to sales organization/compensation structure to better align incentives with fastest-growing product lines

items.notes: Implies ~6-8% YoY growth, up from ~5% growth in FY2025, driven by accelerating Cloud Infrastructure Services and security demand; note this predates the Sept 24, 2026 expanded Anthropic deal, which management said will have minimal FY2026 revenue impact but should support the FY2027 acceleration
Includes an estimated ~$0.12 non-GAAP EPS dilution from the LayerX acquisition

Management flagged significant near-term margin pressure from ramping Cloud Infrastructure Services investment; large CIS contracts are expected to generate 60-70% gross margins and 20-30% operating margins once fully deployed and utilized, but margins compress during the capacity build-out phase
Up from 39% YoY growth realized in Q2 2026 ($99M quarterly revenue); the primary company-specific growth KPI

items.target: ~40% of revenue for FY2026 (Q3 2026: $475M-$525M, ~43-46% of quarterly revenue)
items.notes: A step-change from historical capex intensity (previously well below 20% of revenue), driven by GPU/data-center buildout for Cloud Infrastructure Services and AI customer commitments; ~$5.5 billion of capex specifically tied to the newly expanded Anthropic commitment, to be spent over the term of that multi-year deal
Management commentary tied to the ramp of the Anthropic and other large AI infrastructure commitments signed in 2026; not yet formal guidance

guidance.management_commentary: Management (CEO Tom Leighton) has repeatedly emphasized that Cloud Infrastructure Services is now the company's primary growth engine, citing a sold-out GPU pipeline, continued NVIDIA GPU procurement, and typically a 6-9 month lag between signing large AI infrastructure contracts and revenue recognition. Management characterizes near-term margin compression as an investment phase ahead of an expected 2027 growth and margin inflection as large committed contracts (Anthropic, the robotics customer, and others) ramp to full utilization. The scale of the September 2026 Anthropic expansion (up to ~$20B total potential commitment) represents a strategic bet that Akamai's distributed, edge-oriented compute platform can capture a durable share of AI inference workloads, funded predominantly through convertible debt and equity dilution (warrants) rather than internally generated cash flow.

bull_case: Security remains the largest, highest-growth, most durable revenue category (~53% of revenue, +10% YoY FY2025), providing a profitable core to fund and de-risk the AI/cloud pivot

Landmark AI infrastructure commitments (up to $20B potential with Anthropic, plus other frontier-lab and robotics deals) validate Akamai's distributed edge-compute differentiation and could drive a genuine step-change in growth and scale by 2027 if contracts ramp as guided

Management guidance points to 2027 revenue growth accelerating into the low-teens with large-contract operating margins of 20-30% once capacity is fully utilized, offering a credible margin-recovery path after the current capex/investment trough

25+ years of globally distributed network infrastructure (4,300+ PoPs, ~1,200 network partners) is a genuine, hard-to-replicate asset base underpinning both the legacy delivery/security business and the new edge-AI-inference strategy
Active bolt-on M&A (LayerX, Fermyon, Noname, Neosec) continues to broaden the security and edge-compute product portfolio to stay ahead of evolving AI-era threats and workloads
bear_case: Leverage has ballooned - convertible note principal roughly doubled to $7.64B in a matter of months (May 2026 issuance), a very large debt load relative to ~$4.2-4.5B of annual revenue, funding a still-unproven, capital-intensive cloud/AI compute pivot

Legacy delivery revenue (~30% of total) remains in structural decline with no sign of stabilization, and gross margins have compressed from ~60.4% (FY2023) toward ~55.8-56.1% (H1 2026) as the mix shifts to lower-margin cloud/compute revenue

Extreme customer concentration risk emerging in the new growth engine - a handful of frontier AI labs (chiefly Anthropic, which is now also an Akamai shareholder via warrant) account for a fast-growing and outsized share of contracted future revenue and justify billions in capex; any AI capex slowdown, customer financial distress, or renegotiation would be highly consequential

Near-term capex (~40% of FY2026 revenue, ~$5.5B tied to the Anthropic deal alone) will pressure free cash flow and could require further debt or equity issuance if AI infrastructure demand does not materialize as fast as guided

Akamai remains structurally disadvantaged versus hyperscalers (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure) in raw compute/GPU purchasing power, co-location access, and balance-sheet scale, raising execution risk that the cloud/AI pivot underdelivers relative to the capital committed; the stock's sharp single-session reversal (up ~20%+ after-hours, then down ~6.8% the next session) around the Anthropic news illustrates investor uncertainty about whether the deal economics justify the dilution and capex
